verses.text: Yahweh spoke to Moses, saying,

“Moreover, you shall tell the children of Israel, ‘Anyone of the children of Israel, or of the strangers who live as foreigners in Israel, who gives any of his offspring  to Molech; he shall surely be put to death. The people of the land shall stone him with stones.
I also will set my face against that person, and will cut him off from among his people because he has given of his offspring  to Molech, to defile my sanctuary, and to profane my holy name.
If the people of the land all hide their eyes from that person, when he gives of his offspring  to Molech, and don’t put him to death;
then I will set my face against that man, and against his family, and will cut him off, and all who play the prostitute after him, to play the prostitute with Molech, from among their people.
“‘The person that turns to those who are mediums, and to the wizards, to play the prostitute after them, I will even set my face against that person, and will cut him off from among his people.
“‘Sanctify yourselves therefore, and be holy; for I am Yahweh your God.
You shall keep my statutes, and do them. I am Yahweh who sanctifies you.
“‘For everyone who curses his father or his mother shall surely be put to death: he has cursed his father or his mother; his blood shall be upon him.
“‘The man who commits adultery with another man’s wife, even he who commits adultery with his neighbor’s wife, the adulterer and the adulteress shall surely be put to death.
“‘The man who lies with his father’s wife has uncovered his father’s nakedness: both of them shall surely be put to death; their blood shall be upon them.
“‘If a man lies with his daughter-in-law, both of them shall surely be put to death: they have committed a perversion; their blood shall be upon them.
“‘If a man lies with a male, as with a woman, both of them have committed an abomination: they shall surely be put to death; their blood shall be upon them.
“‘If a man takes a wife and her mother, it is wickedness: they shall be burned with fire, both he and they; that there may be no wickedness among you.
“‘If a man lies with an animal, he shall surely be put to death; and you shall kill the animal.
“‘If a woman approaches any animal, and lies down with it, you shall kill the woman and the animal. They shall surely be put to death. Their blood shall be upon them.

“‘If a man takes his sister, his father’s daughter, or his mother’s daughter, and sees her nakedness, and she sees his nakedness; it is a shameful thing. They shall be cut off in the sight of the children of their people. He has uncovered his sister’s nakedness. He shall bear his iniquity.

“‘If a man lies with a woman having her monthly period, and uncovers her nakedness; he has made naked her fountain, and she has uncovered the fountain of her blood. Both of them shall be cut off from among their people.
“‘You shall not uncover the nakedness of your mother’s sister, nor of your father’s sister; for he has made his close relative naked. They shall bear their iniquity.
If a man lies with his uncle’s wife, he has uncovered his uncle’s nakedness. They shall bear their sin. They shall die childless.
“‘If a man takes his brother’s wife, it is an impurity. He has uncovered his brother’s nakedness. They shall be childless.
“‘You shall therefore keep all my statutes, and all my ordinances, and do them; that the land, where I am bringing you to dwell, may not vomit you out.
You shall not walk in the customs of the nation, which I am casting out before you: for they did all these things, and therefore I abhorred them.
But I have said to you, “You shall inherit their land, and I will give it to you to possess it, a land flowing with milk and honey.” I am Yahweh your God, who has separated you from the peoples.

“‘You shall therefore make a distinction between the clean animal and the unclean, and between the unclean fowl and the clean: and you shall not make yourselves abominable by animal, or by bird, or by anything with which the ground teems, which I have separated from you as unclean for you.
You shall be holy to me; for I, Yahweh, am holy, and have set you apart from the peoples, that you should be mine.
“‘A man or a woman that is a medium, or is a wizard, shall surely be put to death: they shall stone them with stones. Their blood shall be upon them.’”

footnotes.content: The Lord opens this hard chapter by speaking directly to Moses. Even laws that cost lives come wrapped in God's own voice—a reminder that what looks like judgment is meant to be heard as care for the whole people's soul.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Molech was a Canaanite god to whom parents sacrificed their own children. The Lord doesn't hide from this horror—He names it straight and calls it what it is. Some evils deserve to be called by their name, not softened.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Notice: God Himself says 'I will set my face against' the violator. His face—the source of blessing—turns away from those who defile His sanctuary. But His face can also turn toward us in forgiveness. Everything depends on where we turn first.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: A community that looks away from such sin becomes complicit. The text assumes people will be tempted to pretend they didn't see it. We know how easy that is. Sometimes holiness begins with not looking away.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Here's the sorrow of it: not just the guilty person, but the whole household suffers. That's how deeply these choices ripple. The Lord holds this up so we might consider what we invite into our homes and families.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Mediums and wizards claimed to speak to the dead—a perversion of seeking God. The temptation to bypass God and grab answers from anywhere else is ancient. We still feel it: anything but wait and trust.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: After naming the sins, the Lord pivots: 'Sanctify yourselves.' It's not despair, but invitation. Holiness is both God's gift (He sanctifies) and our choice (we sanctify ourselves). We are invited to return.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The Lord doesn't hand us laws and disappear. He stays present: 'I am Yahweh who sanctifies you.' His name, His person, His action—they are one. Obedience is not a test we take alone.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Even in a list of grave laws, cursing one's parents stands. The family is the first place we learn about order, respect, and belonging. To curse those who gave us life is to tear at the root.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Adultery breaks covenant. The Lord takes it seriously because covenant is serious—it's how He loves us. When we teach our children to keep their word, we're teaching them the language of the kingdom.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: To lie with your father's wife is to attack the father's honor and place. These laws protect the bonds that hold a family—and a people—together. Chaos begins when we erase boundaries we were born into.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Daughter-in-law, father-in-law: these are family bonds sealed by covenant. To break them this way is called 'perversion' not because the bodies are wrong, but because the trust is shattered. The Lord cares about the people we're bound to.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: This verse names a grave violation of God's created order. The Lord sees all disordering of His design. We need not soften this or rage about it—we can let it stand as written and ask the Lord to make us wise about His design.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: A man taking both mother and daughter: not just one sin, but a cascade. He has become tangled in deception and appetite that devours whole households. The Lord sees the full shape of it and grieves.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The Lord places all creatures under the sacred order He established. When a man breaks that order, the creature is killed too—not in cruelty, but to mark how far the violation reaches. Nothing is left unchanged by such sin.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The law holds both man and woman equally to account. There is no hiding behind weakness or custom. The Lord's holiness sees through all excuse. And His grace, when it comes, reaches both too.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Seeing nakedness—seeing without shame, without the covering that respect provides. Incest strips away the safe distance that makes family a refuge. He shall bear his iniquity: some weights we carry all our lives.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: To uncover a woman's 'fountain'—her life source—at her monthly time: the text speaks plainly about the body's seasons. God made those seasons. To violate them is to violate a woman's own design, her dignity as one made in His image.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Mother's sister, father's sister: these are the ones who know your story, who carry your family's memory. To uncover their nakedness is to betray that trust and erase the boundary that kin provides.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Uncle's wife: again, the family circle. 'They shall die childless'—a sorrow that echoes. Sometimes the Lord lets the consequence teach what words cannot. Broken covenant closes the door to life's continuation.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Brother's wife: if a man's brother dies, there are laws for his widow. But to take her as the living brother—to turn sacred duty into appetite—is impurity. Line and intent matter. The Lord knows the difference.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: After all the laws, the promise: keep them, and the land will hold you. Obedience and home belong together. When we honor the boundaries God gives, we find we're building a place where we can flourish.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The Canaanites—the nations already dwelling there—did 'all these things.' That's why the land itself 'abhorred' them. The Lord is not inventing holiness here; He's restoring it, turning Israel toward what the land itself knows.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The Lord separates Israel for a purpose: not to make them proud, but to make them His. 'You shall be mine'—that's the whole point of every law. Every boundary is an act of betrothal, a way of saying, 'I have chosen you.'
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Clean and unclean, holy and common—the whole creation is marked by distinctions. Learning to make distinctions is learning to see the world as God does. When we honor what is set apart for us, we practice reverence.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Holy to me; for I am holy. The holiness flows from God toward His people, not the other way around. We don't become holy by earning it; we become holy by standing in the presence of the Holy One and letting Him make us His.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Readers today hear an echo in this final word: the Lord still draws a line between seeking Him directly and seeking through mediums, false teachers, or the voices of the age. The call to go straight to Him—no middleman, no shortcut—still holds.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
